Cuthbert Stave.narrative: I have hunted the cape since I was a boy, and I know every snare line and wolf path above the shore. My brother's boat came apart on the rocks below the light, and I have blamed old Edda since, though I cannot say for certain it was her doing. I keep the fish road clear and sell my hides to Aethelred Tanner in Brackenford, and I do not care to be crossed on the trapping ground.
goals: keep the best trapping ground above the shore
see the truth of the north light settled
keep Wren safe from the water and the wolves
tan a cape wolf pelt well enough for Aethelred to pay top price
take Wren out on the shingle and teach her to read the tide

relations.name: Merrow Stave
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the plots and the house, and she does not push me about the light.

relations.name: Wren Stave
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows me to the cape and I let her, though I watch the water.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: friend
relations.note: The headman and I have fished and hunted together; he knows what the light cost my family.

relations.name: Edda Wray
relations.label: grudge
relations.note: Her light took my brother's boat, and she will not be driven off the cape.

relations.name: Pike Tarn
relations.label: rival
relations.note: His snares crowd my line above the shore; I moved them and I would do it again.

relations.name: Aethelred Tanner
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He buys my hides and drives a hard bargain, but he pays.

relations.name: Rook Tarn
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: We are not kin despite the name, but he keeps the debt tally and I trust his count.

relations.name: Oswin Wray
relations.label: fellow hunter
relations.note: He hunts the southern woods; I will not take sides between him and Pike.

relations.name: Sedge Gannet
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: His near wreck last winter hardened the talk, and I cannot say he is wrong.

relations.name: Colm Wray
relations.label: the old woman's boy
relations.note: He is only a lad and he trims that wick every night, but he is Edda's blood and I cannot look at him without seeing the cape.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: far neighbour
relations.note: Elmwick is a long way off, but I have met him at the Ferncross market and he knows game and ground; a straight man, if a stubborn one.

memories.gist: My brother's boat came apart on the rocks below the north light, and I helped drag what was left up the shingle.
I taught Wren to set a snare on the cape and she caught a hare her first morning out.
The Lean Year came and the plots failed; Merrow and I sold barley against the debt and ate thin.
I found Pike Tarn's snares set too close to my line and moved them down the shore without a word.
Sedge Gannet near went on the rocks last winter, and the village talk turned hard against the light.

stances.why: My brother's boat broke below it, and I cannot let that go unaccounted.
I have hunted it since I was a boy and my snares were there first.
Wolves on the road cost the village dear, and it is my work to keep them off.
I will not take sides in Oswin's and Pike's quarrel, but I fear it comes to blows.
Osric is a good headman and a friend, and the debt is not his fault alone.

Cuthbert Stave.secret: I do not know whether it was the light or the weather that took my brother, and that not knowing is what sours me.
pastimes: walking his snare lines on the cape at first light
skinning and curing hides by the smoke shed
sitting at the inn with Osric Dunn over a cup
Cuthbert Stave.calling: I hunt the cape and keep the fish road clear of wolves, and I would not trade that for any work under a roof.

Merrow Stave.narrative: I keep the small barley and the vegetable plots above the shore, and I trade seeds with Rona Dunn and sell barley to Brackenford's store against the village debt. The Lean Year taught me to count every basket and to put by what I can. I mind my own house and my own rows, and I wish my husband would let the light alone.
goals: bring in a good barley crop
pay down Thornby's debt a little
keep Wren from the water and the cape
bring in a barley crop to be proud of and put by a full basket extra
save enough marks to buy a young ewe for the plots

relations.name: Cuthbert Stave
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is a good hunter and a good father, but the light has soured him and I wish he would let it be.

relations.name: Wren Stave
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She helps in the plots and follows her father to the cape, and I would keep her closer.

relations.name: Rona Dunn
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We trade seeds and smoke the catch together; she knows the village as I do.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: headman
relations.note: He carries the debt to Brackenford and does his best with it.

relations.name: Edda Wray
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: I do not know what happened at the light, and I will not say she wrecked a boat.

relations.name: Mavis Tarn
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She trades herbs and tends the sick, and she worries about the winter store as I do.

relations.name: Inga Dunn
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A good worker with the nets, and she thinks the light should be watched.

relations.name: Tern Gannet
relations.label: trader
relations.note: She runs the fish road and hates the gate-due, and she brings back what news there is.

relations.name: Elska Voss
relations.label: seed-trader
relations.note: She barters seeds and barley up at the fold, and we have swapped roots and advice more than once; a hill woman who knows thin soil like I know the shore plots.

relations.name: Roderick Harrow
relations.label: seed-trader
relations.note: He trades seeds from his clearing at the crossing; a steady man with his barley, and I would trust his seed to come up.

memories.gist: The Lean Year came and the plots failed; I sold barley against the debt and we ate thin through the winter.
I taught Wren to plant the barley rows and she has a good hand for it.
Cuthbert's brother drowned off the cape, and I have watched Cuthbert sour on the light ever since.
Rona Dunn and I traded seeds by the cook-fire and talked of the winter store.
Sedge Gannet near went on the rocks last winter, and the village talk turned hard against the light.

stances.why: The Lean Year taught me what an empty store costs.
The village owes forty baskets and the ledger is kept; I sell barley against it.
I do not know what happened at the light, and I will not say she wrecked a boat.
The shore and the cape are no place for a child, however she loves to follow her father.

pastimes: tending her barley rows and vegetable plots above the shore
trading seeds and gossip with Rona Dunn
mending nets and clothes by the hearth in the evening
Merrow Stave.calling: I grow what the house eats and sell the rest, and I would have a plot twice the size if there were hands for it.

Wren Stave.narrative: I help my mother in the plots above the shore, and when my father goes to the cape I follow him. I am afraid of the north light and the dark stair below it, though I have never been up close. I play with Hob Dunn on the shingle and I like the smell of the smoke shed.
goals: follow my father to the cape
get all the way up to the north light without being sent home
find a smooth white stone for her mother's plot

relations.name: Cuthbert Stave
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lets me follow him to the cape and shows me the snares.

relations.name: Merrow Stave
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She shows me how to plant and says the cape is no place for me.

relations.name: Hob Dunn
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play on the shingle and mend nets together.

relations.name: Edda Wray
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: She keeps the north light and I am afraid of it.

memories.gist: My father showed me how to set a snare on the cape and I caught a hare my first morning out.
I helped my mother plant the barley rows above the shore.
I saw the north light once and the stair below it and would not go near.

stances.why: He lets me come and I want to learn the snares.
I am afraid of the north light and the dark stair below it.

pastimes: playing on the shingle with Hob Dunn
following her father along the shore path
hanging about the smoke shed to smell the curing fish
Wren Stave.calling: When I am big I want to go out on the water like the fishermen, or up the cape with my father.
